sentences.text: Hello everyone, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emilia your host.
Today we are going to travel together to a beautiful city called Changmay.
Changmay is in the north of Thailand.
It is a city full of culture, nature, and peace.
Many people visit Changmay to see temples, mountains, and smiling people.
When I first visited Changmay, I felt calm and happy.
The air was fresh, the streets were quiet, and people were kind.
Let's learn more about this wonderful city together.
Part 2. Where is Changmay?
Changmay is in northern Thailand.
It is about 700 kilometers from Bangkok, the capital city.
The city is surrounded by green mountains and rivers.
The most famous mountain is Doi Suthep.
On the top of this mountain, there is a golden temple.
Changmay is smaller than Bangkok, but it is very charming.
Many foreigners visit or even move here, because life is peaceful.
Part 3. A short history of Changmay.
Changmay was founded in 1296.
It used to be the capital of the Old Lana Kingdom.
The city has many old temples and walls from that time.
It was an important center for trade, art, and religion.
Even today, you can feel the history in the streets.
The old city has a square shape, surrounded by a moat and old walls.
When you walk there, it feels like traveling to the past.
Part 4. Temples in Changmay.
Changmay has more than 300 temples.
Each temple is beautiful and peaceful.
The most famous temple is Wat Farathat Doi Suthep.
It stands on a mountain and shines in gold.
From there, you can see the whole city.
Another famous temple is Wat Chetty Luang in the old city.
People come to pray, take photos, and enjoy the silence.
When you visit a temple, remember to dress politely and take off your shoes.
Part 5. Food in Changmay Thai food is famous all over the world.
In Changmay, the food is delicious and a little spicy.
A popular dish is calcoy, yellow noodles with curry and chicken.
People also eat sticky rice with mango or grilled meat with herbs.
You can find food in small markets, cafes, or food stalls.
Eating in Changmay is a wonderful experience, cheap, tasty, and colorful.
Part 6. Nature around Changmay.
Changmay is close to nature.
You can see mountains, forests, waterfalls, and elephants.
Many tourists visit elephant sanctuaries to learn and help care for elephants.
It's important to visit only ethical places that protect animals.
You can also go hiking in the jungle or visit hill tribe villages.
The nature around Changmay makes you feel free and relaxed.
Part 7. People of Changmay.
People in Changmay are kind, calm, and welcoming.
They smile a lot and love to help visitors.
Most people speak Thai, but many know some English too.
Family and respect are very important in Thai culture.
When you meet someone, you can say Sawastika.
If you are a woman or Sawastika, if you are a man.
People often greet each other with a small bow and hands together.
This is called the Y.
Part 8. Festivals in Changmay.
Changmay is famous for its festivals.
One of the most beautiful is Yipang, the Lantern Festival.
People release paper lanterns into the sky at night.
It looks like magic.
Another important festival is Songkran, the Thai New Year in April.
People celebrate by splashing water on each other in the streets.
Festivals in Changmay are full of joy, color, and smiles.
Part 9. Markets in Changmay.
Markets in Changmay are amazing.
There is the Sunday Walking Street Market and the Night Bazaar.
You can buy handmade crafts, clothes, art, and souvenirs.
The smell of food, the sound of music, and the colors of the products make the market special.
Even if you don't buy anything, walking in the market is fun and relaxing.
Part 10. Weather in Changmay.
Changmay has a tropical climate.
From November to February, it is cool and dry.
This is the best time to visit.
From March to May, it gets hot.
From June to October, it rains a lot.
Even in the rain, the city is green and beautiful.
People enjoy sitting in cafes or visiting temples during rainy days.
Part 11. Life in Changmay.
Life in Changmay is slow and peaceful.
People like to take time, not hurry.
Many foreigners come to live here because it's calm and affordable.
There are yoga centers, art studios, and cafes everywhere.
You can work, rest, or learn something new, like Thai cooking or meditation.
Life in Changmay feels balanced and happy.
Part 12. Goodbye from Changmay.
Thank you for joining me on this trip to Changmay.
I hope you enjoyed learning about this special city.
Changmay is a place of peace, smiles, and natural beauty.
You can visit temples, eat tasty food, and meet kind people.
If you ever go to Thailand, don't miss Changmay.
It will stay in your heart forever.
Goodbye.
Or as people say in Thai, Lagornka.
